Welcome to Week 12 of the NFL season, and Happy Thanksgiving!

The NFL is doing its part to keep marriage counselors in business. Your Thanksgiving weekend schedule: A game on Wednesday night, a triple-header on Thanksgiving Day, a game on Black Friday, and then the usual Sunday-Monday schedule with the remaining slate. Saturday is a day off, but there are wall-to-wall college rivalry games. Eat, drink, and watch football. Then watch more football. What could possibly go wrong?

Game of the Week: There are a few good choices but it has to be Chiefs at Bills on Thanksgiving night. Fun fact: It’s only the second time in NFL history that two teams are coming into a game having won three straight contests by 17 or more points. Mahomes! Allen! Enjoy this one with your second piece of pumpkin pie and a nightcap. The line: BUF -3.

There are four weeks left before the fantasy playoffs start in most formats. Still time to make a move, so read on!

Stats of the Week

  1. Every team in the NFC North is over .500, while no team in the NFC South is over .500.
  2. The Bills’ defense has not allowed a touchdown across 43 straight possessions.
  3. The flip side: Across Weeks 10 and 11, the Cowboys’ offense had a stretch of nine straight possessions that resulted in a touchdown.
  4. Each of the Cowboys’ last two games had more than 80 total points scored.
  5. In all three of their games since trading away DT Jeffery Simmons, the Titans have allowed 40+ points.
  6. Seven different 49ers players who are 30 or older have caught a TD pass this season, the most in NFL history.
  7. In the first half against Philadelphia, Aaron Rodgers averaged one half of an air yard per pass attempt (the lowest total for a half of football since they began tracking air yards in 2006). Rodgers has been benched for Mason Rudolph.
  8. Dak Prescott was the No. 1 fantasy QB this past week, and CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens were the No. 1 and No. 2 fantasy wide receivers.

Bye Weeks: NONE

Week 12 Rides, Fades and Sleepers

For those who are familiar with this column, you know the drill. For everyone else: The Rides, Fades, and Sleepers is an analysis of players that I think are primed for an especially strong or poor performance, often as compared to consensus expectations. This isn’t a straight-up Start/Sit exercise. As a general rule, start your studs. I’ll rarely list the most obvious names at a position as “Rides” because those players are almost always expected to have strong performances. You don’t need me or anyone else telling you to start CeeDee Lamb. While this analysis is intended for season-long play, it works for DFS formats too. Half PPR scoring and Expert Consensus Rankings (ECR) are used for the column.

Each week, I’m picking a Ride, Fade, and Sleeper of the Week. The rules: The Ride of the Week can’t be a truly elite option, the Fade can’t be someone who nobody is starting anyway, and the Sleeper must be an actual sleeper, from down in the rankings.

Last week, my Rides, Fades, and Sleepers did well, with a lot more hits than misses throughout. Ride of the Week Tony Pollard went over 100 yards rushing but didn’t score or do anything in the passing game, so that’s a bit of a miss. Fade of the Week Tyler Warren had one catch. Sleeper of the Week Justin Herbert was the QB4 on the week, with two passing TDs, a rushing TD, and no picks. You can check my work here.

***

Ride of the Week: Bucky Irving (vs. CAR). Bucky is on one. He’s recorded six straight games with at least 18 carries and racked up six TDs across his last four outings. For what seems like the hundredth time in the last two seasons, Baker Mayfield is playing hurt – and he can’t do his usual Baker stuff. Plus, without Mike Evans he’s not the same QB. Tampa is pounding the ball and playing solid defense, and this is a home game, in primetime, that they absolutely must have. Irving should once again feast, in a plus matchup. Carolina has allowed the second most fantasy points per game (FPPG) and the most rushing touchdowns (14) to opposing backs. ATop-3 RB finish this week is realistic.

Fade of the Week: Jaylen Warren (vs. DEN). Don’t look now, but Warren has reverted to a timeshare back on a sputtering offense. After an epic run before the bye, it’s been back-to-back stinkers (a total of 16 carries for 43 yards). He does have seven catches in those two contests, and that’s the path to success this week – doing a little of what Ashton Jeanty did to the Broncos catching passes out of the backfield a week ago. It’s viable, as Denver has allowed the most receiving yards to opposing backs. I’m not buying it. Mason Rudolph isn’t likely to check it down as much as Aaron Rodgers. It’s getting ugly in Pittsburgh. I’m out.

Sleeper of the Week: I’ll preface all sleeper discussions by saying it’s harder to find sleepers this week, with no teams on bye. Managers are less likely to need to reach. With that said, I’ll go with Deshaun Watson (vs. LV), who I think is a good start this week in 2-QB formats. Watson has been OK for fantasy this season (QB19 in FPPG). He’s starting to run a little more and has some very good young weapons to throw to. The Raiders have allowed the fifth most FPPG and the second most TD passes (23) to opposing QBs, and Cleveland is a tough place to visit. Watson is ranked as the QB15 this week and I think a Top-12 (QB1) finish is in play.

Quarterback:

Elite options this week – Josh Allen, Patrick Mahomes, Dak Prescott, and Joe Burrow;the analysis starts below them.

Rides:

Three QBs ranked in the Top-10 this week who I think will outperform projections: Jayden Daniels (@ARI), Trevor Lawrence (vs. TEN), and C.J. Stroud (vs. BAL). All have good matchups. Lawrence is coming off a rough outing at New York and gets a very soft landing against what is now the NFL’s most generous defense this side of Dallas. Daniels is starting to look like he did in his rookie year (and is again pulling games out of his you-know-what), and Stroud has been humming for weeks and gets a team whose season effectively ended on Sunday. Ride these three with confidence.

Other Rides in the Top 15: Kirk Cousins (vs. ATL, in a bit of a revenge game) and Jared Goff (vs. CHI in the game with by far the highest Vegas total of the week – 55.5).

Sleepers:

J.J. McCarthy (vs. IND) has been steering the ship and limiting his mistakes. The Colts are probably the NFL’s hottest mess right now, and McCarthy should find little in the way of resistance. Indy allows the tenth most FPPG to opposing QBs, but they’ve been worse during their recent collapse.

Joe Milton (@DAL) has done little to inspire confidence since he became the Birds’ starter a few weeks ago. A date with Dallas on Thanksgiving is his best opportunity to show off that rifle arm and running ability. I wouldn’t start him over any of the really good QBs, but I like his chances to finally put up decent QB2 numbers. Dallas has allowed the second most points in the NFL, and the fourth most FPPG to opposing QBs.

Other QB2-types to consider if you need it: Geno Smith (@MIA), Sam Darnold (@SF), and Justin Herbert (vs. NE, assuming he plays).

Fades:

I don’t have a ton of confidence in either Jordan Love (@LAR) or Matthew Stafford (vs. GB) in the Wednesday night game. The defenses in this game rank sixth and seventh in terms of FPPG allowed to opposing QBs, and with Micah Parsons set to make his season debut, both QBs could be under constant pressure from very good defenses that can get to the QB. Love has weapons but his team can’t run the ball. Stafford is missing his go-to receivers. This game has a Vegas total of 44.5 and I think it’ll go under.

QB2s who managers could be considering, but who I’d avoid if I could: Anthony Richardson (vs. NYG, who have been making QBs pay lately), Michael Penix, Jr. (@MIN, in an awful road matchup), Jacoby Brissett (@HOU), Bryce Young (@TB), Tommy DeVito (@LAC), and Fernando Mendoza (@CLE).

Running back:

Elite options this week – Jahmyr Gibbs, James Cook, Bijan Robinson, Christian McCaffrey, andEmmett Johnson (yes, you heard that right); the analysis starts below them.  

Rides:

Backs in smash spots this week:

Chase Brown (vs. NO). Despite another struggle in Week 11, Brown is set up to succeed in a rebound game for the Bengals, against a defense allowing the third most FPPG to opposing RBs. He continues to see enough work in the passing game to make him viable even when the rushing isn’t there.

Saquon Barkley (@DAL). He keeps gutting it out and I don’t think this arm/neck injury will keep him out of the Thanksgiving game. He has a rushing TD in four straight contests, despite just 50 rushing attempts in that span. Dallas can’t stop anyone on the ground or through the air. They’ve allowed the most rushing yards and FPPG to the position. For as long as Barkley is in the game, he should romp.

Cam Skattebo (@IND). The backflip probably annoyed his coach, but this is a great matchup, and a game New York should dominate. The Colts allow the ninth most FPPG to opposing backs.

Others ranked inside the Top-25 this week who I think have a good shot to outperform their weekly projections: Kyren Williams (vs. GB, and I think he’ll bounce back and be busy in the passing game), Breece Hall (@MIA), Ollie Gordon II (vs. NYJ), and Quinshon Judkins (vs. LV).

Sleepers:

It’s hard to find sleepers at RB this week. If Kenneth Walker plays, I think Emmett Johnson is Flex-worthy as they won’t want to overwork the starter.

A few lower-end options (outside the weekly Top-25) to consider if you’re stuck: David Montgomery (vs. BAL, and even if Woody Marks is back, I think he’ll dominate touches and especially near the goal line), Rhamondre Stevenson (@LAC), and in the same game Omarion Hampton (vs. NE), Aaron Jones, Sr. (@ATL), Braelon Allen (@MIA), and Jacory Croskey-Merritt (@ARI).

If you’re stuck, I think you can reach for Kenneth Gainwell (vs. CAR) and Chris Rodriguez, Jr. (vs. TEN).

There’s a chance that D’Andre Swift spends a little time in the doghouse for losing another fumble last week, giving Kyle Monangai (@DET) a more prominent role for the time being, albeit in a very tough matchup. Monangai didn’t look fully healthy in his return last week, so I’d be careful.

Fades:

Dear Jonathan Taylor (vs. NYG), I’m glad I don’t roster you anywhere because I know how hard it is to sit a player of your talent. But look at the last month and try not to puke. His fantasy points in Half PPR: 4.7, 6.9, 11.3, and 4.7, with zero TDs in that span. That’s Jonathan Freaking Taylor! Game script and organizational dysfunction are an awful combo and they’re killing him. He’s ranked outside the Top-20 this week and he’s a sit for me, unless I’m out of decent options.

I’m nervous about D’Andre Swift (@DET) this week, as discussed above. The Lions allow the fourth fewest FPPG to opposing RBs and I can’t shake the fumble punishment concerns with Ben Johnson.

Travis Etienne, Jr. (@CIN) did get better volume this week, but a lack of usage in the passing game and Alvin Kamara’s propensity to get the value touches are concerning. He’s a Fade for me.

I’m avoiding all Packer RBs (@LAR) on Wednesday night. It’s a committee no matter who plays, they don’t run the ball well, and the Rams are stingy, allowing the second fewest FPPG to opposing backs.

Other RB Fades: Zach Charbonnet (@SF) and Arizona RBs (vs. WAS).

Wide receiver:

Elite options this week – Jaxson Smith-Njigba, Ja’Marr Chase AND Tee Higgins, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Justin Jefferson, and CeeDee Lamb; the analysis starts below them.

Rides:

Here are seven Rides this week, all pretty obvious names, and all ranked inside the weekly Top-20: Parker Washington (vs. TEN, most yards and FPPG allowed to opposing WRs), Nico Collins (vs. BAL), Malik Nabers (@IND), Luther Burden III (@ DET), and in the same game, Jameson Williams (vs. CHI), Chris Olave (@CIN), and DeVonta Smith (@DAL, fourth most FPPG allowed to opposing receivers).

Moving down in the rankings, I think these players in the WR 21-30 range this week are good bets to beat their weekly projections: Rashee Rice (@BUF), Tet McMillan (@TB), K.C. Concepcion (vs. LV), Rome Odunze (@DET), and Ladd McConkey (vs. NE, allowing the second most FPPG to opposing WRs, but only if Justin Herbert plays).

Sleepers:

WRs ranked outside the Top-30 this week that I think you can plug into lineups if you’re in need include: Jakobi Meyers (@TEN), Caleb Douglas (vs. NYJ, to bounce back), Pat Bryant (@PIT), Chimere Dike (vs. JAC), Antonio Williams (@ARI), and if you want a real boom/bust play, Tank Dell (vs. BAL).

Fades:

Garrett Wilson (MIA) is getting harder to trust. Geno is spreading the ball around and he isn’t always getting the massive target share of prior seasons. Miami is also a surprisingly tough matchup. They held Wilson to 2-26-0 in Week 7 (in a game the Jets trailed much of the way) and they’re allowing the fourth fewest FPPG to opposing WRs.

You can’t, and shouldn’t, sit Mike Evans (@SEA). Just know that it’s the single-worst matchup for WRs. The Seahawks have yielded the fewest yards and FPPG and just five TDs to receivers on the season, and Evans is always a re-injury risk.

D.J. Moore (vs. KC) is another one you can’t sit, but he got banged up against Miami and it’s a short week. The Chiefs have allowed the fewest TDs to opposing receivers (just three, in ten games) and the second fewest FPPG.

I’ll continue to fade both Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin (vs. CAR). I just don’t like what I’m seeing from this passing offense and its banged-up quarterback.

Weekly PSA: Don’t start any Colts or Cardinals receivers.I’ll give Kyle McCord one more week before I add the Dolphins to this list.

Other WRs ranked inside the Top-30 and/or who have been starting options this season and who I’m lower than consensus on this week include: Jaylen Waddle (@PIT, and it’s very concerning that his snap share is around 50% most weeks), Jalen Coker (@TB), Carnell Tate (@JAC), Tre Tucker (@CLE), Roman Wilson (vs. DEN), and Germie Bernard (vs. DEN, and he’s droppable at this point).

Tight end:

Elite options this week – Brock Bowers (if he plays), Trey McBride, George Kittle, and Isaiah Likely; the analysis starts below them.

Rides:

I like all of these TEs who are ranked inside the weekly Top-12 to beat their projections: Colston Loveland (@DET, most FPPG and TDs allowed to the position, although they’ve improved lately), Harold Fannin, Jr. (vs. LV), Travis Kelce (@BUF, in a game that could have a lot of points), T.J. Hockenson (vs. ATL), and Chig Okonkwo (@ARI).

Sleepers:

There are several names to consider this week.

Michael Mayer (@CLE) is in play, and especially if Brock Bowers is out.

item.title: Chicago Bears week 12 game preview: Detroit Lions Thanksgiving Day
item.description: The Bears and Lions are set for a huge Thanksgiving clash. @SamHouseholder has the game preview.
item.content:encoded:
A clash of 8-2 teams to kick off Thanksgiving Day.

This isn’t your run-of-the-mill early mid-2010s Detroit Lions-Chicago Bears matchups anymore.

This game has significant weight in the NFC North battle and playoff seeding.

Gone are the days of quarterbacks whose mere names elicit groans, first-round busts, offenses that are offensive in the bad way and defenses that can’t stop a cold.

No, this is a meeting of two great coaches and two outstanding quarterbacks, each with a bevvy of weapons lined up around them.

This game is why our fanbases have endured all the bad, the jokes, the frustration.

We’ve longed for the days when we could sit down and expect the team to win. To be in primetime games that made the collective NFL world say, “I can’t wait to watch the Lions-Bears game.”

Thursday is that day.

Now the Cowboys game is when you want to eat, because the games on the other side of it are the good ones.

Enjoy this one. Win or lose, it should be a good one. The Bears badly need a division win.

Detroit Lions

SB Nation site:Pride of Detroit

Record: 8-2, first in the NFC North

Last week: 31-21 winagainst the Buccaneers

Game day, time, TV: Thursday, noon CT, FOX

Spread: Bears -1.5

Bears all-time record against: 105-82-5

Historical meetings: Sunday, Nov. 26, 1933, the 6-2-1 Bears hosted the 6-3 Portsmouth Spartans at Wrigley Field.

Jack Manders kicked things off with a first-quarter field goal. Later in the quarter, Bill Hewitt threw a 34-yard pass to Bill Karr for a touchdown. 

The Spartans came back with Glenn Presnell hitting Ernie Caddel twice for touchdowns in the second quarter and again in the fourth.

But the Bears would finish it off with a 29-yard Bronko Nagurski run to win 17-14.

Last meeting: Week 18 last season. In a slugfest game, the Lions took a 16-0 lead on three field goals and a Jared Goff-to-Jahmyr Gibbs touchdown pass. 

The Bears woke up in the fourth quarter, with Caleb Williams hitting Jahdae Walker for a 25-yard score and converting a 2-point conversion on a Kyle Monangai run.

Then, Williams hit Colston Loveland for another TD and converted the game-tying 2-point conversion with a pass to Cole Kmet.

Kevin Byard picked off Goff on the next Lions’ drive, but the Bears took an intentional grounding penalty that set them back to third and 20. They ended up punting back to Detroit. 

The Lions moved the ball down the field and Jake Bates hit a walk-off 42-yard field goal for a 19-16 Detroit win.

Injury report: The Lions listed four players on their estimated injury report for Tuesday. (The full game day report will be out later today, so stay tuned and we’ll share it later.)

Limited

  • S Chuck Clark (hamstring)

Did not participate

  • DT Skyler Gill-Howard (knee) – announced out for the season
  • CB Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (shoulder)
  • DE DJ Wonnum (back)

Offense: The Lions offense comes in ranked fifth in points and third in yards. 

Detroit’s passing offense ranks fifth and their rushing offense ranks eighth.

Jared Goff (67.8 pct cmp/2,716 yds/20 TD/4 INT) should probably be higher in MVP conversation than he is currently. He’s playing as well as Joe Burrow, Brock Purdy and Josh Allen.

And he still has a great group of talent around him. Amon-Ra St. Brown (70 rec/792 yds./8 TD), TE Sam LaPorta (39/477/3), Jameson Williams (36/611/6) and Isaac TeSlaa (13/225/1) are making plays up and down the field.

But the main weapon is Jahmyr Gibbs (222 att./1,098 yds./13 TD on the ground and 45/404/2 as a receiver). Gibbs leads the league in rushing attempts, yards, touchdowns and first downs. And in total touches and yards from scrimmage. He’s averaging 109.8 rushing yards per game and his 15 total TDs leads the league as well. 

Defense: Detroit’s defense has improved drastically throughout the season and enters the week 14th in points and 15th in yards allowed.

Their passing defense ranks 27th, while their rushing defense ranks sixth.

Without Aidan Hutchinson, D.J. Wonnum (7 sk/7 TFL10 QB hits/2 PD) is now the pass-rushing leader for Detroit. Alim McNeill (6.5 sk/7 TFL/12 QB hits/1 PD) and Derrick Moore (4.5 sk/4 TFL/8 QB hits) are just behind.

Chuck Clark (61 tkls/2 TFL/4 PD/2 INT/2 FF) is their leading tackler and ballhawk. LB Derrick Barnes (49 tkls/6 TFL/4 QB hits/3 sk/1 INT/2 PD) is making plays all over the field.

In the secondary Roger McCreary (42 tkls/11 PD/1 FF/1 INT/1 sk) and D.J. Reed (42 tkls/3 TFL/7 PD/1 INT) are trying to slow down opposing receivers.

Key match ups: This is going to be a great game between two 8-2 teams and it’s really anyone’s guess what’s going to happen.

The Bears have been playing like they’ve been waiting for this moment. The Lions have just become a rock-solid team, checking off opponents. 

This game is likely going to come down to the trenches. Can the Bears DL slow down Gibbs and pressure Goff? Can the Bears OL open running lanes for Swift and Monangai? 

Which QB will make the fewest mistakes? 

Chicago’s secondary is going to have its hands full with Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. If those guys get free, it could be a long afternoon. 

This game could be 45-43 or it could be 17-14, I really don’t know.

Key stats

  • Since their week six bye, the Lions defense has improved significantly. They allowed 404 yards per game over the first five games, but have allowed just 249 yards per game in the five games since. But the competition has shifted too. The first five game stretch included the Bills, Jacoby Brissett Cardinals and Panthers. Since the bye it’s been the pre-Kirk Vikings, Dolphins, Patriots (who lost Maye in the game) and Bucs.
  • The Lions rank 28th in defensive takeaways with nine on the season. They have just two fumble recoveries and seven interceptions. Their offense has only turned the ball over seven times, which is the second fewest giveaways.
  • The Bears have 19 giveaways, which is the fifth-most in the league. That includes nine lost fumbles by the offense, which is the third-most in the NFL.
  • Chicago and Detroit are about even in plays per drive (fourth and third, respectively) at 6.3 (CHI) and 6.4 (DET). They are also about even in average drive time (3 minutes even for CHI, 2:58 for DET).
  • The Bears have run the third-most plays in the league (714), while the Lions are 13th with 668.
  • Despite having the league’s leading rusher and averaging nearly 110 yards per game by himself, the Lions rank 10th with 132.2 rushing yards per game, while the Bears are third with 142.4 yards per game as a team.

Will the Bears win their first division game of season and get Ben Johnson a win over his mentor? What’s it going to take for Chicago to get the W?

item.title: Houston Texans NFL Power Rankings: Week 12
item.description: Where do the Texans land after their big win over the Colts?
item.content:encoded:
Oh, back for your power rankings fix again? Last week, the Texans inched a hair closer to the AFC playoff bubble with a 26-3 victory over the division rival Indianapolis Colts. Then, on Sunday, they got another boost when the Pittsburgh Steelers stunned much of the NFL crowd by losing to the 2-7 (now 3-7) Philadelphia Eagles, creating an even bigger crack in the postseason door for the Texans to sidle through.

Be it luck or Houston progressing to the mean after an exceptionally unlucky opening month to the season, the Texans are still not dead yet with a record of 4-6, and the road to a winning record seems to just be getting easier and easier. A few weeks ago, New England Patriots QB Drake Maye suffered a fractured fibula while getting sacked during their week 10 tilt against the Detroit Lions, meaning backup, Italian Stallion QB Tommy DeVito will be shouldering the burden of keeping the Pats inside the playoff bubble – something I don’t think a soul in the NFL is expecting. Then, just several hours ago, a nuclear bomb drops in the shadow of night: the Pittsburgh Steelers announced that they are benching QB Aaron Rodgers in favor of backup QB Mason Rudolph for their Friday afternoon match against the Denver Broncos! Now, whether or not Rudolph starting over Rodgers is a boon for the Texans remains to be seen, but I think we all know what to expect out of Mason Rudolph, and it’s not much. This is a move from the Steelers that’s screams desperation, which is great news for a surging Texans team that will be visiting Pittsburgh in just two weeks!

And so, two more puzzle pieces fall into place for the Houston Texans, who will need to capitalize on this good fortune by taking care of business this Sunday against the 4-7 Baltimore Ravens. Their recent loss to the Carolina Panthers and the fact that their starting QB is journeyman Jacoby Brissett may give you some confidence going into Sunday, but do not be fooled by this Texans team: they can lose to anybody. Knowing our luck, that Ravens vs. Texans match on Sunday will probably end up as a shootout, where whoever has the ball last wins the game. As with all of the other wins the Texans have earned this year, this game will require another banner performance from CJ Stroud in order for Houston to improve to 5-6, which will get him another step closer to All-Pro status, or even an MVP trophy! If there’s one thing we can be thankful for this Thanksgiving, it’s CJ Stroud keeping this team in the mix.

Can it be done? Can Stroud keep the ball rolling? Can the Texans take advantage of this road to the postseason emerging in front of them? Well, maybe the power rankings will give us an idea of their chances!Here’s where the Texans are ranked after their big win over the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday night:

NFL.COM:

15. Houston Texans (4-6) (Last Week: 17)

I can’t quit the Texans and neither can you! Houston dominated Indianapolis on Thursday night, moving to 4-6 and — thanks to Pittsburgh’s upset loss to Philadelphia on Sunday — preserving its playoff hopes. Those hopes can move closer to becoming reality if the Texans can take down the Steelers two Sundays from now.

– Nick Shook

ESPN:

16. Houston Texans (4-6)

Week 11 result: Beat the Colts 26-3
Week 11 ranking: 16

Extension candidate: QB C.J. Stroud

Through 10 games of Stroud’s fourth season, he is up to 2,656 passing yards, 22 touchdowns and only four interceptions. He is on pace to throw for 4,515 passing yards and 37 touchdowns, both of which would be career highs. And his Total QBR (73) is fifth best in the NFL. Stroud has earned the payday he bet on himself for. Now, it comes down to whether the Texans are willing to pay whatever that price is. They’re not expected to balk at Stroud’s offers, but if they do, things could get interesting

– DJ Bien-Aime

SPORTS ILLUSTRATED:

16. Houston Texans (4–6) 

Last week’s ranking: No. 20
Last week’s result: beat Colts, 26–3
This week: vs. Ravens

If you loved the feature on the Texans’ vegetable score on Amazon Prime last week, read the story from where it came…all the way back in August. 

– Conor Orr

BLEACHER REPORT

20. Houston Texans (4-6)

Last Week: 22

Week 11 Result: Won vs. Indianapolis 26-3

The Houston Texans aren’t done yet.

The win came against a struggling Colts team, but it was one Houston needed to stay on the fringes of playoff contention.

Whether they make the playoffs or not, quarterback C.J. Stroud appears to have earned a second contract. After a fifth game in the last seven with a passer rating north of 100, Stroud told reporters he hopes to finish the season strong and get the Texans into the postseason for a fourth straight year.

“Always things you can clean up so we’ll do that when the time is necessary,” he said, “but I think you got to enjoy it, and it will be a couple of good weeks for us, so we got to go 1-0 mentality the rest of the time.”

Houston won nine straight to make the playoffs last year after a 3-5 start. It will take a similar run this year—the Texans can afford maybe one more loss the rest of the way.

– Gary Davenport

CBS SPORTS:

18. Texans (4-6) (Last Week: 19)

After beating up the Colts, they are once again eyeing the last playoff spot. But they can’t afford any more missteps the rest of the way.

– Pete Prisco

USA TODAY:

21. Houston Texans (23): Maybe you could say their playoffs have already begun. The Texans will certainly need to knock off the Ravens and Steelers the next two weeks if they want to have a shot of playing into mid-January.

– Nate Davis

YAHOO! SPORTS:

17. Houston Texans (4-6, LW: 18)

David Montgomery could finally make a big impact for the Texans. In his return from injury, he rushed for 107 yards on 26 carries against the Colts. Indianapolis isn’t a good team but it was still nice to see something positive from Houston’s running game, even if it was in a blowout.

The Texans have been looking for consistency all season, but it’s not too late for them to rally for a wild-card spot in a weak race. Their Week 13 game at the Steelers will be a big one for the Texans’ playoff hopes. For now, Houston hopes a dominant win over Indianapolis is the start of a streak.

“It’s huge,” quarterback C.J. Stroud said, according to the team’s site. “I think this is a start to something that we need to go on a run with.”

– Frank Schwab

THE ATHLETIC:

21. Houston Texans (4-6)

Last week: 23

Thursday: Beat Colts 26-3

Something to be thankful for: A running game

Houston had 167 yards on the ground Thursday, its highest total since Week 18 of the 2024 season. David Montgomery returned to the lineup after missing four games with a groin injury and had 107 yards, his best output as a Texan. “I think we can be really, really good (on offense),” Montgomery told reporters afterward. “It’s never too late to find your stride.”

Up next: vs. Ravens, Sunday, 1 p.m. ET

– Chad Graff & Josh Kendall

PRO FOOTBALL TALK:

19. Texans (No. 22; 4-6): C.J. Stroud is back. Will the defense ever be able to say the same thing?

– Mike Florio

Average Ranking: 18.11 (Last Week: 20.00)

It looks like some pundits are starting to feel the Texans mojo once again, but others are still feeling burned from the Texans deflating appearances against the New York Giants and Cleveland Browns a few weeks ago. In both of those weeks leading up to the games, the Texans rose in most power rankings as the vast majority of analysts and football fans thought they were due for a win streak, and in each of those moments, Houston came up short. What makes this upcoming game any different? Well, I think Frank Schwab of Yahoo! Sports and Chad Graff & Josh Kendall of The Athletic nailed it: RB David Montgomery and the run-blocking:

David Montgomery’s return to action against the Colts allowed offensive coordinator Nick Caley to run a more balanced offense, and when the Texans can get going on the ground, they’re incredibly hard to beat. RG Ed Ingram, rookie LG Keylan Rutledge, and C Evan Brown had some of their best performances of the season against the Colts on Thursday night, clearing open holes for Montgomery to rush and (somewhat) successfully eliminating Colts DT Grover Stewart and LB Bryce Boettcher from most plays. If they can manage a similar performance against the Ravens this Sunday, they should be able to control the pace of the game, but if not, we’ll be relying on this wishy-washy defense to make a play against the gunslinging Jacoby Brissett, who is almost guaranteed to throw over 35 passes against the Texans.

What do you think, though? Will we be thankful for the dawn of another Texans win streak, or will we be drowning our sorrows in Thanksgiving leftovers and pumpkin pie Sunday night? Well, regardless if Houston wins or loses, I’ll be going after that pumpkin pie, but a win would make the retreat to sweets a little less depressing than if it were following another critical loss. Let us know what your thoughts – or what you’ll be eating – down in the comments below!

Go Texans!

item.title: Five field goals, a primetime game-winner, and now a weekly NFL award for Commanders rookie Drew Stevens
item.description: The undrafted rookie went 5-for-5 on field goals—including the walk-off winner—in Washington’s 22-20 Monday night victory over Cincinnati, setting two franchise rookie records in the process
item.content:encoded:
When the Washington Commanders lined up for a 26-yard field goal as time expired on Monday Night Football against the Cincinnati Bengals, I didn’t feel the usual knot in my stomach that has defined white-knuckle football in Washington for the better part of a decade. Watching undrafted rookie Drew Stevens line up his fifth kick of the night, I had total confidence he was going to split the uprights.

As it turned out, my confidence was well-placed. Stevens drilled the game-winner to seal a 22-20 Week 11 victory, and the NFL officially recognized his primetime clinic by naming him the NFC Special Teams Player of the Week.

Stevens’ honor is the first of his young NFL career and makes him the first Washington player to take home the weekly award since Austin Seibert did it back in Week 2 of the 2024 season. More importantly, it validates what we saw on the field Monday night: a rookie who simply refuses to blink when the lights are brightest.

Against Cincinnati, Washington’s offense moved the ball well—piling up 428 total yards—but repeatedly stalled once it crossed into Bengals territory, going just 1-for-4 in the red zone. Whenever a drive bogged down, Dan Quinn called on Stevens, and the 22-year-old out of Iowa answered every single time. He finished a perfect 5-for-5 on field goals (connecting from 36, 40, 25, 41, and 26 yards) and 1-for-1 on extra points, accounting for 16 of Washington’s 22 points. His 41-yarder tested his nerve against swirling wind, while his final 26-yard chip shot carried all the pressure of a walk-off winner after rookie receiver Antonio Williams made two clutch late catches to set up the attempt.

With that performance, Stevens etched his name into the franchise record books twice in one night:

  • Single-Game Rookie Record: He became the first rookie in Washington history to make five or more field goals in a single game.
  • Season Milestone: He became the first rookie kicker in franchise history to reach 22 made field goals in a season since Charlie Gogolak in 1966—and Stevens did it in just 10 games.

To truly appreciate how refreshing this is, you have to remember the seemingly endless kicking carousel Washington fans have endured. Since moving on from Dustin Hopkins, the franchise has cycled through roughly a dozen kickers—from Joey Slye and Cade York to Austin Seibert, Zane Gonzalez, Greg Joseph, Matt Gay, and Jake Moody. Whether it was Seibert’s 2024 hip and hamstring injuries derailing a promising start, Gay’s struggles in 2025, or persistent inconsistency on long-range kicks, special teams stability at the position remained elusive. Even entering training camp this summer, the job was up for grabs until Stevens decisively outkicked Moody (going 43-of-48 in camp compared to Moody’s 36-of-47) to claim the spot.

After starting his NFL career 3-of-5 through his first two games—with all three of his season’s misses coming from 50-plus yards—Stevens has caught fire. He has now connected on 19 of his last 20 field goal attempts, bringing his season mark to an impressive 22-of-25 (88%) with a long of 57 yards.

For years, every fourth-down decision inside the opponent’s 35-yard line felt like a roll of the dice in Ashburn. Now, with a poised, big-legged rookie who already owns franchise records and a Player of the Week trophy (and a Rookie of the Week nomination) before Thanksgiving, Washington finally appears to have found its long-term answer at kicker.

Next up for Stevens and the 4-5-1 Commanders is a Week 12 road trip to face the Arizona Cardinals—and for the first time in a long time, fans can watch field goal units jog onto the field without holding their breath.

item.title: By the numbers: Rams’ Matthew Stafford in November
item.description: The Rams need Matthew Stafford to be baseball version’s of Mr. November
item.content:encoded:
Matthew Stafford has developed a reputation for playing some of his best football as the NFL season gets deeper and deeper into the calendar. For the Los Angeles Rams, November has provided plenty of opportunities for the veteran quarterback to showcase his experience, elevate his game and help position the team for a postseason push.

Since joining the Rams in 2021, Stafford has put together an impressive collection of numbers during the month of November. Through the Rams’ November games in 2026, he has appeared in 19 games during the month, compiling an 11-8 record as the team’s quarterback.

Here is a look at Stafford’s November production since arriving in Los Angeles:

Matthew Stafford’s November stats (2021–2026):

  • Win-loss record: 11-8
  • Completions/Attempts: 410-of-642 (63.8%)
  • Passing yards: 4,552
  • Passing touchdowns: 41
  • Interceptions: 14

Perhaps the most impressive aspect of Stafford’s November production is his ability to generate touchdowns while limiting turnovers. Across those 19 appearances, he has thrown nearly three touchdowns for every interception, demonstrating his ability to take care of the football while continuing to push the ball downfield.

His November numbers have also improved considerably over the years. In 2021, Stafford threw five touchdowns and five interceptions in three November appearances. In 2022, he was limited to two appearances, throwing three touchdowns without an interception. By 2024, he had accumulated 1,129 passing yards and eight touchdowns in four November games.

His most productive November as a Ram came in 2025. Stafford completed 106 of 159 passes for 1,207 yards, 15 touchdowns and just two interceptions across five games. That production included four consecutive victories to begin the month.

Stafford has continued that success in 2026, throwing five touchdowns and three interceptions while completing 64.9% of his passes through three November appearances.

As the Rams prepare for the final stretch of the regular season, Stafford’s historical November production offers another reason for optimism. At 38 years old, the veteran quarterback continues to demonstrate that experience matters when the stakes get higher and the season begins to wind down.

item.title: Devontez Walker wins AFC special teams player of the week
item.description: The Ravens didn’t beat the Panthers on Sunday, but they did have one individual do enough to win a player of the week award.
item.content:encoded:
The Ravens didn’t beat the Panthers on Sunday, but they did have one individual do enough to win a player of the week award.

The NFL named returner Devontez Walker special teams player of the week.

Walker had an 86-yard kickoff return for a touchdown in the second quarter of the contest. He ended up returning seven kicks for 211 yards, becoming the second player to have at least 200 kickoff return yards in a game this season.

His touchdown return was just the second kick returned for a TD this season.

This is Walker’s first player of the week award.
